core.name: Check for updates
core.summary: Check whether a newer PlotJuggler release is available. When installed extensions have updates, an UPDATE button appears in the title bar. The check on startup can be turned off.
core.entry_point: Help → Check for Updates...; startup check: File → Preferences... → Appearance → Check for updates on startup:

core.name: Cloud data sources
core.summary: Browse and download recordings kept in a cloud service. Each service is provided by a cloud extension and appears in the Cloud tab of the Sources panel once installed.
core.entry_point: Sources panel → Cloud → choose the service in the list → + (Open cloud browser)

core.name: Custom Series
core.summary: Create new series computed from existing ones, such as math on one or more series or a script, in the Transform Editor. Custom series are listed in their own panel and can be edited or deleted there. Built-in filters can also be applied to the curves of a plot from that plot's right-click menu (Apply Filter...).

core.name: Datasets panel
core.summary: Every loaded file or stream is a dataset, listed with its topics and fields as a tree. The filter box searches by name, three buttons show or hide plot series, 2D image topics and 3D scene topics, and right-clicking a dataset offers Info, Merge, Reload, Replace and Remove.
core.entry_point: Datasets panel → Filter... box; right-click a dataset for its options

core.name: Diagnostics
core.summary: Errors and warnings from PlotJuggler and its extensions, such as a file that failed to load or a plugin that could not start, are collected in one list that can be filtered by level and source.

core.name: Extensions Marketplace
core.summary: Browse, install, update, disable and remove extensions: data loaders, streaming sources, message parsers and toolboxes. An extension can also be installed from a local ZIP file. The Help menu lists the extensions installed.
core.entry_point: File → Extensions Marketplace…; installed list: Help → Installed Extensions

core.name: Layouts
core.summary: Save and reload the whole workspace: tabs, plots, custom series and markers. When saving, the layout can be bound to the loaded data so that loading it opens the same files again.
core.entry_point: File → Save Layout... / Load Layout...; recent layouts: Sources panel → Recent layouts & files

core.name: Live streaming
core.summary: Plot data while it arrives from a live source. The sources come from streaming extensions (for example MQTT, ZeroMQ, UDP or ROS 2). A stream can be paused, and the buffer length sets how many seconds of data are kept. With some sources a topic only starts receiving data once it is dropped into a view.
core.entry_point: Sources panel → Stream → choose the source in the list → + (Start streaming)

core.name: Open data files
core.summary: Load recorded data from a file. The formats that open depend on the data loader extensions installed (for example CSV, MCAP, ULog or Parquet). Each loaded file becomes its own dataset, and several can be loaded side by side.
core.entry_point: File → Open Data File..., or Sources panel → File → Load a data file

core.name: Playback
core.summary: Replay loaded data over time: play and pause, loop, change the speed and step the time cursor. Plots, images and 3D views follow the cursor.
core.entry_point: Bottom bar: Start/Stop player (Space), Loop, Rate (speed multiplier), Step size

core.name: Plot tabs, splits and XY plots
core.summary: Organise plots in tabs and split a plot area into several. Drag series from the Datasets panel onto a plot to show them. An XY plot draws one series against another.
core.entry_point: + on the tab bar adds a tab; plot area toolbar (shown when you hover the top edge of a plot): Split horizontally / Split vertically / Fullscreen; XY plot: drag two series from the Datasets panel with the right mouse button onto an empty plot

core.name: Preferences
core.summary: Settings for the appearance, plotting, the 2D and 3D scenes, extra plugin folders and the Marketplace registry, and recording.
core.entry_point: File → Preferences... (pages: Appearance, Plotting, Scene 2D, Scene 3D, Plugins, Recording)

core.name: Record streams to MCAP
core.summary: While streaming, record what the active streams receive into standard MCAP files, one file per stream, so the session can be opened again later. The folder is set in Preferences, on the Recording page.
core.entry_point: Sources panel → Stream → record button (Record the subscribed topics of every active stream, one MCAP file per stream)

core.name: 3D scene
core.summary: Show 3D data in step with the time cursor: coordinate frames (TF), point clouds, occupancy grids, robot models (URDF and meshes) and markers.
core.entry_point: Empty plot area: click the 3D button (cube icon), then drag 3D topics from the Datasets panel onto it

core.name: Source timeline: align and merge datasets
core.summary: Shows each dataset as a bar on a shared time axis. Dragging a bar shifts that dataset in time, Align lines up the starts of all datasets, and merging combines the selected datasets into one.
core.entry_point: Title bar → Toggle bottom panel → source timeline: drag a bar, Align, Merge the selected datasets; also Datasets panel → right-click → Merge

core.name: State Transitions
core.summary: Show text, integer and true/false series as coloured strips of states over time, for example a robot's mode or a status flag.
core.entry_point: Empty plot area: click the State Transitions button, then drag the series from the Datasets panel onto it

core.name: 2D viewer for images, video and depth
core.summary: Show camera images, video and depth images from the data in step with the time cursor, with annotations drawn on top. Depth images are shown with a colour map.
core.entry_point: Empty plot area: click the 2D button (image icon), then drag an image topic from the Datasets panel onto it

limitations.summary: Loaded data cannot be edited: individual values cannot be changed or deleted, and the original file is never modified. A whole dataset can only be reloaded, replaced, merged or removed.
Enabling or disabling an extension, and adding or removing a custom plugin folder, takes effect only after PlotJuggler is restarted.
A live stream cannot be merged with other datasets while it is streaming; it has to be stopped first.
PlotJuggler 4 only receives and displays data; it cannot publish messages or send commands back to a robot or device.
Not every live source can be recorded: a stream whose extension writes its data directly instead of passing the raw messages to PlotJuggler is left out of a recording.

loaded.name: CSV Loader
loaded.summary: Data loader for CSV files.
loaded.entry_point: Sources panel → File (or File → Open Data File...)

loaded.name: MCAP Loader
loaded.summary: Data loader for MCAP files and split ROS 2 bags (metadata.yaml). Supports ROS1, ROS2, Protobuf, and JSON message encodings.
loaded.entry_point: Sources panel → File (or File → Open Data File...)

loaded.name: Parquet Loader
loaded.summary: Data loader for Apache Parquet files. Efficient columnar storage format.
loaded.entry_point: Sources panel → File (or File → Open Data File...)

loaded.name: ULog Loader
loaded.summary: Data loader for PX4 ULog files. Flight log format for PX4 autopilot.
loaded.entry_point: Sources panel → File (or File → Open Data File...)

loaded.name: MP4 Loader
loaded.summary: Open .mp4 video files and play them in sync with your plots. When a file records its creation time, the video is placed at that wall-clock time; several files can be opened at once.
loaded.entry_point: Sources panel → File (or File → Open Data File...)

loaded.name: 3D Loader (PLY/PCD)
loaded.summary: Open static 3D files: .pcd files and vertex-only .ply files load as point clouds, .ply files with faces load as meshes. Each file is a single snapshot, not a time series.
loaded.entry_point: Sources panel → File (or File → Open Data File...)

loaded.name: Dummy Streamer
loaded.summary: Generates synthetic sine, cosine, sawtooth, and noise signals for testing and demonstration.
loaded.entry_point: Sources panel → Stream → Dummy Streamer → + (Start streaming)

loaded.name: Foxglove Bridge
loaded.summary: Stream live ROS data from a Foxglove WebSocket server, such as foxglove_bridge running on your robot (the same server Foxglove Studio connects to).
loaded.entry_point: Sources panel → Stream → Foxglove Bridge → + (Start streaming)

loaded.name: PlotJuggler Bridge
loaded.summary: Connect to PlotJuggler Bridge server for generic data streaming over WebSocket.
loaded.entry_point: Sources panel → Stream → PlotJuggler Bridge → + (Start streaming)

loaded.name: WebRTC Video Client
loaded.summary: Watch live H.264 camera video from a WebRTC (WHEP) server such as mediamtx, go2rtc, LiveKit or Cloudflare Stream, next to your plots. Each camera reconnects on its own, and the cameras on a mediamtx server can be discovered automatically.
loaded.entry_point: Sources panel → Stream → WebRTC Video Client → + (Start streaming)

loaded.name: ROS CDR Parser
loaded.summary: Decodes ROS 1 and ROS 2 messages, with definitions in .msg or IDL form, into plottable fields. Common sensor and visualization messages (images, point clouds, occupancy grids, grid maps, TF, markers, and yolo_msgs detections as image annotations) are shown in the 2D image and 3D scene views.
loaded.entry_point: No panel of its own: chosen as the message format inside the data source that uses it (for example a stream's message serialization selector).

loaded.name: Protobuf Parser
loaded.summary: Decodes Protocol Buffers messages into plottable fields. Standard Foxglove message types (point clouds, images and compressed video, image annotations, scene entities, transforms, poses, camera calibration, voxel grids and grids) are shown in the 2D image and 3D scene views.
loaded.entry_point: No panel of its own: chosen as the message format inside the data source that uses it (for example a stream's message serialization selector).

loaded.name: JSON Parser
loaded.summary: Message parser for JSON, CBOR, MessagePack, and BSON encoded data.
loaded.entry_point: No panel of its own: chosen as the message format inside the data source that uses it (for example a stream's message serialization selector).

loaded.name: DataTamer Parser
loaded.summary: Decodes data recorded or streamed with the DataTamer logging library into plottable series.
loaded.entry_point: No panel of its own: chosen as the message format inside the data source that uses it (for example a stream's message serialization selector).

loaded.name: Quaternion to RPY
loaded.summary: Converts quaternion (x, y, z, w) time series into Roll, Pitch, Yaw angles with optional unwrapping and degree/radian output.
loaded.entry_point: Toolbox menu → Quaternion to RPY

loaded.name: Transform Editor
loaded.summary: Create named custom series computed from one or more existing signals with Lua functions, like the Custom Series editor of PlotJuggler 3.
loaded.entry_point: Custom Series panel → + (Add custom series)

loaded.name: Mosaico Cloud Server
loaded.summary: Browse Mosaico cloud servers and import their data: filter by metadata with Lua expressions, choose a time range, and stream several topics at once. Install the Arrow IPC Parser alongside it to decode scalar topics.
loaded.entry_point: Sources panel → Cloud → Mosaico Cloud Server → + (Open cloud browser)

loaded.name: Arrow IPC Parser
loaded.summary: Decodes Apache Arrow IPC data, which carries its own schema, into plottable series. Needed by sources that deliver Arrow data, such as the Mosaico Cloud Server.
loaded.entry_point: No panel of its own: chosen as the message format inside the data source that uses it (for example a stream's message serialization selector).

loaded.name: Assistant Agent
loaded.summary: A chat assistant inside PlotJuggler: ask about your topics and signals, get their statistics, and have it create its own derived series, markers and plot tabs. It uses the Claude Code or Codex command-line tool already installed and signed in on your machine; the plugin stores no API keys. Linux, macOS and Windows.
loaded.entry_point: Toolbox menu → Assistant Agent

loaded.name: ROS 2 Topic Subscriber
loaded.summary: Subscribe to ROS 2 topics in real time and stream the decoded fields into PlotJuggler.
loaded.entry_point: Sources panel → Stream → ROS 2 Topic Subscriber → + (Start streaming)
